Simplified ideas

The big ideas of the knowledge base, each drawn in a few pictures. Open an idea and use the arrows to step through it, one picture at a time. Tap a picture to enlarge it.

ALearning by correcting mistakesChapter 2 · 5 pictures

A network begins by guessing. Each guess is compared with the right answer, the gap is measured, and the weights are nudged to shrink it. Repeat that many times and the guesses get better.

1 / 5

Read it in Chapter 2 · 2.2 Backpropagation revived

BHow a model picks the next wordChapter 4 · 4 pictures

A language model reads the words so far, weighs which ones matter most, scores every candidate for the next word, picks one, and then starts again with the longer sentence.

1 / 4

Read it in Chapter 4 · 4.6 Self-attention and the transformer

CSounding right is not being rightChapter 5 · 6 pictures

A chatbot writes fluent answers from patterns it learned, not from a store of facts. Without sources there is a gap between an answer that sounds right and one that is right. Sources help close it, and you still check.

1 / 6

Read it in Chapter 5 · 5.5 Why hallucination happens

DWhat a weight isChapter 5 · 6 pictures

A weight is a number that says how strongly one unit influences another. Training adjusts billions of them until the model predicts well, then freezes them. Open-weight models let you download that finished set.

1 / 6

A simplification. A model’s weights encode patterns learned from its training data, not a list of stored facts.

Read it in Chapter 5 · 5.2 Weights inside a language model

EThe dials behind an image modelChapter 5 · 5 pictures

An image generator has a few settings that change what you get. Some set how closely the picture follows your prompt, how much of a starting image survives, and how many refining steps run. Others were fixed in training, or are yours to choose each time.

1 / 5

The percentages are for picturing the idea. Real tools show these settings on their own scales, such as a guidance number, a strength value and a step count.

Read it in Chapter 5 · 5.6 Images from noise: diffusion

FAssistant, model, engine, hardwareChapter 6 · 4 pictures

An assistant is the product you talk to, built from instructions, tools and skills. Underneath it, machinery runs the model: the model holds the learned weights, the engine is the software that runs it, and the hardware is the chips and servers.
